analysis.title: The market purge is not over
key_insights: Goldman's Privorotsky says hedge funds are unwinding AI longs and systematic strategies are taking losses. Goldman's Equity Systematic L/S estimate fell 2.17% last week, its worst weekly drawdown since December 2023.
Fundamental L/S net exposure is back at the 7th percentile, largely because of index short covering. Single stocks have been sold for seven consecutive weeks and retail sentiment is deeply bearish.
Goldman's risk indicator had one of its largest monthly declines in October. It is not yet at contrarian buy levels, which start below -1.
After the 11 largest declines in Goldman's RAI since 2005, the S&P 500 returned -17% to +7% over one month and -32% to +18% over six months. A positioning reset does not guarantee a bottom.
Investors entered the latest panic heavily short vol, were squeezed, and then bought protection at much higher prices.
Single-stock volatility and credit markets have priced stress for weeks while index volatility lagged. Goldman's Garrett says that gap is starting to close as macro equity volatility catches up.

SPX 12-month implied correlation is near 20%, among the lowest readings in history. The options market is pricing another year of extreme dispersion in 2027. A sudden correlation spike could turn single-stock volatility into an index-level volatility shock.

Upside volatility in some of the largest stocks defined 2026. Per Garrett, downside volatility is now taking over and short-dated skew is repricing to reflect it. Downside protection is becoming more expensive.
JPMorgan's Market Intelligence team notes the S&P 500 has been positive 6, 9 and 12 months after every midterm election since 1990, averaging +11.4%, +12.5% and +14.7%.

JPMorgan says the recent de-risking is not yet capitulatory, with quant selling and elevated tech positioning still posing risks. Momentum exposure is down to 30% of its peak, and with widespread hedge fund deleveraging JPMorgan sees the ingredients for an alpha rebound.
risk_factors: Systematic and quant selling may not be finished.
A sudden spike in correlation could lift index volatility toward the level of single-stock volatility.
Downside tail risk is rising as short-dated skew reprices.
Elevated tech positioning remains a risk, per JPMorgan.
Historical outcomes after large RAI declines are wide, with one-month S&P 500 returns from -17% to +7%.

tension_points.bull_case: JPMorgan sees momentum exposure at 30% of peak and widespread hedge fund deleveraging setting up an alpha rebound. S&P 500 gains after every midterm since 1990 averaged +11.4% at 6 months.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's risk indicator is not yet below -1. Quant selling and elevated tech positioning remain, and past large RAI declines were followed by one-month returns as low as -17%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's risk indicator staying above -1 while systematic selling continues would mean the reset is not finished.
